Diamond Pricing Analysis

Kenny Ejiogu

2026-08-24

Project Overview

This project analyzes the diamonds dataset included with ggplot2 to explore how diamond characteristics are associated with price. The analysis focuses on carat weight, cut quality, color, and clarity while demonstrating data exploration, visualization, aggregation, and regression in R.

Research Questions

  1. How is diamond price distributed across the dataset?
  2. How strongly is carat weight associated with price?
  3. How does median price vary across cut quality?
  4. How well can carat and cut explain variation in diamond price?

Data Preparation

diamond_data <- ggplot2::diamonds %>%
  select(carat, cut, color, clarity, depth, table, price, x, y, z) %>%
  drop_na()

glimpse(diamond_data)

Summary Statistics

diamond_summary <- diamond_data %>%
  summarise(
    observations = n(),
    average_price = mean(price),
    median_price = median(price),
    average_carat = mean(carat),
    median_carat = median(carat)
  )

diamond_summary

Visualization 1: Distribution of Diamond Prices

ggplot(diamond_data, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 500, color = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Diamond Prices",
    subtitle = "Price distribution across more than 50,000 diamonds",
    x = "Price",
    y = "Number of Diamonds"
  )

Visualization 2: Carat Weight and Price

ggplot(diamond_data, aes(x = carat, y = price, color = cut)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.20, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(group = 1),
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  labs(
    title = "Diamond Price Increases with Carat Weight",
    subtitle = "Each point represents one diamond; color indicates cut quality",
    x = "Carat Weight",
    y = "Price",
    color = "Cut"
  )

Visualization 3: Median Price by Cut

price_by_cut <- diamond_data %>%
  group_by(cut) %>%
  summarise(
    median_price = median(price),
    average_price = mean(price),
    diamond_count = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(median_price))

ggplot(price_by_cut, aes(x = reorder(cut, median_price), y = median_price)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Diamond Price by Cut Quality",
    subtitle = "Comparison of typical prices across cut categories",
    x = "Cut Quality",
    y = "Median Price"
  )

Visualization 4: Price by Carat Range

carat_bands <- diamond_data %>%
  mutate(
    carat_group = case_when(
      carat < 0.50 ~ "Under 0.50",
      carat < 1.00 ~ "0.50-0.99",
      carat < 1.50 ~ "1.00-1.49",
      carat < 2.00 ~ "1.50-1.99",
      TRUE ~ "2.00+"
    ),
    carat_group = factor(
      carat_group,
      levels = c("Under 0.50", "0.50-0.99", "1.00-1.49", "1.50-1.99", "2.00+")
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(carat_group) %>%
  summarise(
    median_price = median(price),
    count = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(carat_bands, aes(x = carat_group, y = median_price)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Price by Carat Range",
    subtitle = "Larger carat groups show substantially higher typical prices",
    x = "Carat Range",
    y = "Median Price"
  )

Statistical Analysis

price_model <- lm(
  price ~ carat + cut,
  data = diamond_data
)

summary(price_model)

Model Fit

model_fit <- tibble(
  r_squared = summary(price_model)$r.squared,
  adjusted_r_squared = summary(price_model)$adj.r.squared
)

model_fit

Key Findings

  • Diamond prices are strongly associated with carat weight.
  • The price distribution is right-skewed, with fewer observations at the highest prices.
  • Median prices differ across cut categories, but cut should be interpreted alongside carat because diamond size has a major influence on price.
  • Carat-based price bands show a clear increase in typical price as diamond size increases.
  • The regression model quantifies the relationship between carat, cut quality, and price.

Because this is an observational dataset, the analysis identifies associations rather than causal relationships.
